listen.explanationKey: What did the civil rights movement do?
facts: The civil rights movement fought to end racial discrimination.
Martin Luther King, Jr. was a leader of the movement. He worked for equality for all Americans.
He hoped people would “not be judged by the color of their skin, but by the content of their character.”

newWords.meaning: treating people unfairly because of who they are
being treated the same as everyone else
keeping people apart because of their race
the work in the 1950s and 1960s to end segregation and discrimination

listen.explanationKey: What major event happened on September 11, 2001 in the United States?
facts: On September 11, 2001, terrorists attacked the United States.
They took over planes. Two crashed into the World Trade Center in New York City, one into the Pentagon in Virginia, and one in a field in Pennsylvania.

newWords.meaning: a person who uses violence to make people afraid

help.simpler: On that day, the country was attacked by terrorists.
help.example: A terrorist uses violence against people to scare them.
help.why: The test asks what happened on September 11, 2001.

story.say: They took over planes.

help.simpler: The terrorists took control of passenger planes.
help.example: They took over four planes that day.
help.why: This is part of the answer on the test.

story.say: Two planes crashed into the World Trade Center in New York City.

help.simpler: Two planes hit the World Trade Center towers.
help.example: The World Trade Center was in New York City.

story.say: One plane crashed into the Pentagon, in Virginia.

help.simpler: One plane hit the Pentagon.
help.example: The Pentagon is the building of the Department of Defense.
help.why: This is another answer on the test.

story.say: One plane crashed in a field in Pennsylvania.

help.simpler: The last plane came down in a field.
help.example: It crashed in Pennsylvania, not at its target.
help.why: This is another answer on the test.

help.example: Every year on September 11, Americans remember the people who died.

listen.explanationKey: Why did the United States enter the Persian Gulf War?
facts: In 1990, Iraq invaded its small neighbor, Kuwait. In 1991, the United States led many countries in the Persian Gulf War to force the Iraqi military out of Kuwait.
On September 11, 2001, terrorists from a group called al-Qaeda attacked the United States. Their leaders were hiding in Afghanistan.
So the United States began a war in Afghanistan in 2001. This was part of the War on Terror.
In 2003, the United States also went to war in Iraq.

newWords.meaning: a country's army and other armed forces

story.say: In 1990, Iraq invaded its small neighbor, Kuwait.

help.simpler: Iraq’s army went into Kuwait to take it over.
help.example: Kuwait is a small country next to Iraq.
help.why: This led to the Persian Gulf War.

story.say: In 1991, the United States led many countries in the Persian Gulf War.

help.simpler: The United States and many other countries fought together.
help.example: The Persian Gulf is the sea near Iraq and Kuwait.
help.why: The test asks why the U.S. entered this war.

story.say: The war forced the Iraqi military out of Kuwait.

help.simpler: The war made Iraq’s army leave Kuwait.
help.example: To force means to make someone do something.
help.why: “To force the Iraqi military from Kuwait” is the test answer.

check.prompt: Why did the United States enter the Persian Gulf War?

listen.explanationKey: Name one example of an American innovation.
facts: An innovation is a new idea or invention.
American innovations include the light bulb, the automobile, the airplane, skyscrapers and the assembly line.
In 1969, Americans were the first people to land on the moon.

newWords.meaning: something made for the first time

help.simpler: An innovation is something new that people make or think of.
help.example: An invention is a new thing someone makes.
help.why: The test asks you to name one American innovation.

story.say: American innovations include the light bulb and the automobile.

help.simpler: The light bulb and the car are American innovations.
help.example: An automobile is a car.
help.why: “Light bulb” and “automobile” are answers on the test.

story.say: The airplane is an American innovation too.

help.simpler: Americans made the first airplane flight.
help.example: The Wright brothers flew it in 1903.
help.why: “Airplane” is an answer on the test.

check.prompt: Name one example of an American innovation.

help.simpler: Americans were the first people to walk on the moon.
help.example: They flew there in a spaceship called Apollo 11.
